<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par59 />{{Hyphenated word end|junctive|conjunctive}} accent, as {{GHGheb|text=הֹרָ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=עָנָ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=15}} (where, however, the reading {{GHGheb|text=עָנַ֫נִי}} is also found). With a sharpened {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}}: {{GHGheb|text=דָּנַ֫נִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=6}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִסְרַ֫נִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=18}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|59|g}}
3. The 3''rd sing. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלַת}} (={{GHGheb|text=קָֽטְלָה}}) has the twofold peculiarity that (''a'') the ending ''ath'' always takes the tone,<ref>{{GHGheb|text=חִבְּלָֽתְךָ֣}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=5}} is an exception. {{GHGheb|text=כֶם}} would probably even here have the tone (see e); but no example of the kind occurs in the O.T. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=2}} the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} is used instead of the {{GHGterm|perfect}} with a suffix.</ref> and consequently is joined to those suffixes which form a syllable of themselves ({{GHGheb|text=נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=ךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=נוּ}}), without a connecting vowel, contrary to the general rule, {{GHGpar|58|f}}; (''b'') before the other suffixes the connecting vowel is indeed employed, but the tone is drawn back to the ''penultima'', so that they are pronounced with shortened vowels, viz. {{GHGheb|text=־֫ ־ֶךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־֫ ־ַם}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲהֵבָ֫תֶךְ|translate=she loves thee}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=15}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=גְּנָבָ֫תַם|translate=she has stolen them}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=32}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׂרָפָּ֫תַם|translate=it burns them}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=48|verse=7}}. For {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ תְנִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ תְךָ}} &c., in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=־ָֽ תְנִי}} is found, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=10}}, and {{GHGheb|text=־ָֽ תְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=5}}; and also without the {{GHGterm|pause}} for the sake of the assonance {{GHGheb|text=חִבְּלָֽתְךָ}}, ''she was in travail with thee'', ibid. The form {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלַ֫תּוּ}} (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=15}}) has arisen, through the loss of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} and the consequent sharpening of the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} (as in {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נּוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נָּה}} for {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נְהוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נְהָ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|58|i}}), from the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלַ֫תְהוּ}}, which is also found even in {{GHGterm|pause}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֲהֵבַֽתְהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=28}}; elsewhere it takes in {{GHGterm|pause}} the form {{GHGheb|text=סְמָכָֽתְהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=16}}); so {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלַ֫תָּה}} from {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלַ֫תְהָ}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=6}}; in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=15}}, always, on the authority of Qimḥi, without {{GHGterm|Mappiq}} in the {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, which is consequently always a mere vowel-letter.

{{GHGmargin-letter|59|h}}
4. In the 2''nd sing. masc.'' the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתָּ}} is mostly used, and the suffixes have, therefore, no connecting vowel, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=זְנַחְתָּ֫נוּ פְרַצְתָּ֑נוּ|translate=thou hast cast us off, thou hast broken us down}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=60|verse=3}}; but with the suff. of the 1st sing. the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתַּ֫נִי}} is used, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חֲקַרְתַּ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=1}}; in {{GHGterm|pause}}, however, with {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עֲזַבְתָּ֑נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=2}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=1|verse=15}} (with {{GHGterm|Zaqeph qaṭon}}); but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=צְרַפְתָּ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=17|verse=3}} with ''Mer<sup>e</sup>kha''.—In the 2''nd sing. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=־תִּי}} is also written defectively, {{GHGheb|text=רִמִּיתִ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=15|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=4|verse=9}}. Occasionally the suffix is appended to the ordinary form {{GHGheb|text=־ְתּ}}, viz. {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁבַּעְתָּ֫נוּ|translate=thou}} ({{GHGterm|fem.}}) ''dost adjure us'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=5|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=17.20}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=27}}, and, quite abnormally, with {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} {{GHGheb|text=הוֹרַדְתֵּ֫נוּ|translate=thou}} ({{GHGterm|fem.}}) ''didst let us down'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=18}}, where {{GHGheb|text=הוֹרַדְתִּ֫נוּ}} would be expected. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=וְיִסְּרֵ֫נִי}} is probably intended as an {{GHGterm|imperfect}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|59|i}}
5. In verbs ''middle ē'', the ''ē'' remains even before suffixes (see above, c), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲהֵֽבְךָ֫}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=16}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲהֵבַ֫תְהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=28}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=22|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְרֵא֫וּהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=37|verse=24}}. From a verb ''middle ō'' there occurs {{GHGheb|text=יְכָלְתִּיו|translate=I have prevailed against him}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=13|verse=5}}, from {{GHGheb|text=יָכֹל}} with ''ŏ'' instead of ''ō'' in a syllable which has lost the tone ({{GHGpar|44|e}}).<section end=par59 />

<section begin=par60 />{{GHGpar-heading|60|Imperfect with Pronominal Suffixes}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|a}}
In those forms of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} Qal, which have no afformatives, the vowel ''ō'' of the second syllable mostly becomes {{GHGheb|text=־ְ}} (simple {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ mobile}}), sometimes {{GHGheb|text=־ֳ}}; thus in the principal {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=35|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=62|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=35|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=10}}; before the principal {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=33}}; before a secondary {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=23}}; even before a conjunctive accent, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=23|verse=5}}. Before {{GHGheb|text=־ְךָ}},<section end=par60 /><noinclude>
